As Baku listens to the rules he finds a way to exploit leap second. Now the rules of dropping the handkerchief and the general situation of the game is as follows.
General rules

The game is played with two players and a referee, in this game the two players are “Baku Madarame” also known as just “Baku”, and “Kiruma Souichi” also known as “Leader” or “Hal”, the referee is “Yakou”
The one who drops the handkerchief is “D”, the one who checks the handkerchief is “C”. Both players take turns playing each role
A turn is limited to 1 minute. During that time, “D” and “C” have to drop and “Check” once
If “C” finds the handkerchief, “C” wins. Otherwise “C” loses
If “C” succeeds
the time before the handkerchief is found is called “squandered time” will be added to “C”’s cylinder container
if the cylinder container is filled up to the max capacity of 5 minutes, it’ll be injected into the body immediately
If “C” fails
add one minute of “near death drug” into the cylinder container, and then empty out the container and inject it all into the body
Near death
After injecting the “near death drug” and confirming that the heart has stopped start timing the “squandered time”
After the “squandered time” is up, inject the “revival drug” into the body and start CPR for 10 seconds
After reviving “C”, the match will continue as soon as possible
the guideline for how much near death you can survive is
total near death above 5 minutes will be a guaranteed death
the more times you experience near death, the less chance of revival, so if it's your first time a revival is likely, as you do more cycles of death and revival the chances decrease

each near death is coupled with a small predetermined amount of rest, in the case of a failed check the time spent until the next round is for 1 minute of near death 5 minutes, although it can change with the amount of near death and the amount of near death adds to the 5 minutes of time until next round, and for a successful check it will take 2 minutes until next round regardless of when the check succeeded
Violation of the rules
the following acts will be treated as “unable to continue the match” and lose
committing any violent acts or damaging the devices
not “Dropping” or “Checking” within one minute
Any action that stalls the game
Not following the referees instructions
Winning conditions
the opponent can’t continue the game

The game is played in a singular room on top of a tower and in that room there is a chair in the middle. The floor has special coating so the sound of dropping the handkerchief can not be heard, there are also lights from every angle so the shadows of the opponent can’t be seen. Meaning you can't see or hear the opponent if he is behind you. The person who checks sits in that chair and turns around when they want to check, the person who drops is not restricted in any movement, but is generally advised to stay behind the person checking as if they are in front of them its obvious what the dropping side is doing to the checking side, although this may be used to the D sides advantage by confusing the enemy which we may see later.

The game is based on the ticking clock, every send it makes a click sound and every change of a minute creates a tick sound. The players can count how many clicks there are to know the current time, the tick sound acts as the limit of the round, all players need to turn / check or drop within that time.

From these rules Baku finds a loophole to exploit Leap second. He realizes that in this game something called the safe strategy can be made. Basically because the dropper needs to drop the handkerchief within one minute, if the person who is checking really doesn’t want to fail a check they can turn around as the clock signals the end of the minute to guarantee a check. Baku also knows that the ticking clock will signal the end of a minute twice when it's time for the leap second, the ticking clock will go “tick” for every second that passes and to mark the end of every minute it will make a “Pon“ sound, but in 9AM of this day the ticking clock will go “tick” for 8:59:59, “Pon” for 8:59:60 and another “Pon” for 9:00:00. Meaning there will be two Pon’s. Because Yakou stated during the rule explanation that the ticking clock is absolute and the game timing will be determined by the ticking clock, Baku knew if the ticking clock said there were two ends to a minute he knew it would pass.

Baku realized that he can make Souichi fail a safe strategy if the turn where Baku will drop was exactly aligned to leap second. Souichi who is unaware of leap second, had a check turn that started from 8:59 and wanted to pull a safe strategy then he would turn around as the ticking clock makes the Pon sound but Baku can drop the handkerchief in the second Pon sound and make Souichi fail a check even though he turned around when it had already been 60 seconds and Baku can not be disqualified for breaking the rules as he can drop the handkerchief in the next Pon and claim he dropped the handkerchief exactly one minute, since the ticking clock defined a minute not as 60 seconds but as 61 seconds due to leap second.
